Suggest coalescing in the UI (customer_name || booking_number) or ensuring home.py populates customer_name for the overdue list the same way bounced/unassigned do.

critical_code_review_comments: The spec called the Home v2 response 'kpis/projects/attention' but the implementation uses 'totals' + 'counts' (plus projects + attention + collections_12m + spark + recent). The frontend Home.jsx consumes totals/counts correctly, so this is just a naming divergence from the request copy — flagging only for doc consistency, no code change needed.

routers/project_setup.py: PUT with strictly-typed sections (StrictModel) means roundtripping GET→PUT with the raw bundle fails (plans has 'catalogue' key, pricing has 'rate_card', etc.). The frontend ProjectSetup.jsx handles this correctly by sending only the stripped fields ({project_sequence}, {assignments}, {block_rates}). Documented in test_phase_11b.py so future agents don't repeat my first-run mistake.

home.py builds the 'overdue' list from db.demands but relies on each demand doc carrying customer_name — some demands have it missing/null and the UI renders 'undefined'. Defend in the API or in Home.jsx.

AppShell data-testid coverage is thorough: nav-home, nav-projects, nav-customers, nav-bookings, nav-payments, nav-settings, sidebar-toggle, quick-new, user-menu, menu-logout all resolve. All 10 project tabs and all 27 cat-type-* buttons have testids.
